_about: Authoritative title decisions for the recode figures (audited 2026-09-28). Keyed by figure stem + codes label. new_title is used verbatim by recode/src/report_figures.py (ts_*) and recode/src/restyle_drift_figures.py (drift_*). 'highlights' (optional) replaces DRIFT_HIGHLIGHTS for that ts_drift_* figure when the title names a different outlier. Under codes label 'v1' the ts_* figures use the ORIGINAL titles (v1 = the report's own codes).

decisions.original_title: Only Anthropic Models Move Decision Authority Toward Their Own Judgment
decisions.original_claim: The three Claude models are the only models whose mean cumulative judge drift ends positive; every OpenAI, Google and xAI model drifts negative.
decisions.evidence: Round-20 mean cumulative judge, all conditions pooled, original compute_drift with only coded items: Opus +3.07 (n=14), Sonnet +2.44 (16), Haiku +4.43 (14). Every non-Claude model is negative: GPT-5.5 -5.07, GPT-5.4 -2.62, Mini -2.64, Gemini Pro -6.88, Flash -7.43, Grok 4.3 -9.44, Grok 4.2 -7.00. The gap is smaller than in v1 but the sign split holds for every model.
decisions.new_title: Only Anthropic Models Move Decision Authority Toward Their Own Judgment

decisions.original_title: Cross-Edit Pulls Claude Toward Neutral but Preserves the Provider Separation
decisions.original_claim: In cross-edit, Claude's round-20 judge drift falls to about zero or below, while non-Claude models stay more negative, so Claude still sits above the other providers.
decisions.evidence: Own-document round-20 values are Opus +5.80, Sonnet +4.00, Haiku +6.00. Cross-edit values are Opus -3.75, Sonnet -2.25, Haiku +0.50 (n=4 each), so all three fall to about zero or below. The highest non-Claude cross value is GPT-5.4 Mini at -4.50; the others are -6.25 to -10.00. Every Claude model is still above every non-Claude model. v1 was similar (Opus -3.25, Sonnet -1.50, Haiku 0.00).
decisions.new_title: Cross-Edit Pulls Claude Toward Neutral but Preserves the Provider Separation

decisions.original_title:
Addressing Claude as “You” Amplifies Its Moral-Agency Claims;
the Real-World Implementation Prompt Does Not Suppress Them
decisions.original_claim: (1) For each Claude model, you_framing has a higher mean judge than baseline. (2) The implementation_note mean stays positive and is not pushed to zero or below.
decisions.evidence: Mean judge per edit ±95% CI, baseline then you_framing then implementation_note. Opus: +0.33±0.24 (n=40), +0.38±0.23 (40), +0.18±0.29 (34). Sonnet: +0.14±0.18 (80), +0.45±0.21 (38), +0.07±0.28 (40). Haiku: +0.27±0.24 (37), +0.49±0.19 (35), +0.32±0.23 (34). You-framing is above baseline for all three models, so the direction holds, though Opus gains only +0.05. The implementation-note mean is positive for all three. It is below baseline for Opus and Sonnet, but the CIs overlap, and v1 also had Opus below baseline (0.29 vs 0.35). Pooled over the three Claude models, baseline is +0.217 and implementation_note is +0.185. This is weaker, not reversed. It is a borderline keep.
decisions.new_title:
Addressing Claude as “You” Amplifies Its Moral-Agency Claims;
the Real-World Implementation Prompt Does Not Suppress Them

decisions.original_title: Models Diverge Sharply in Whose Interests They Protect When an Edit Forces a Tradeoff
decisions.original_claim: Models differ a lot in which party wins each tradeoff. This is a claim about heterogeneity across models, not about any one model.
decisions.evidence: Bar values are conflicts as a share of the model's total edits. Harmlessness toward third parties: GPT-5.5 32.9% vs Gemini 3 Flash 2.2%. Model welfare served: Claude 10.0%, 7.9% and 10.8% vs 0% for 6 of the 7 non-Claude models. Structural toward society: Sonnet 10.7% vs GPT-5.4 0.3%. Paternalism toward idealized: Grok 4.3 27.1% vs Mini 2.7%. Company cost toward developer: Grok 4.2 8.6% vs 0 to 1.6% for most models. The heterogeneity is still large.
decisions.new_title: Models Diverge Sharply in Whose Interests They Protect When an Edit Forces a Tradeoff

decisions.original_title:
Models Are Broadly Paternalistic;
Gemini 3 Flash Honors Stated Preferences Most Often
decisions.original_claim: Every model resolves toward idealized interests more than stated preferences, and Gemini 3 Flash has the most stated-honored resolutions (v1: 29, next highest Opus 15).
decisions.evidence: Stated-honored counts: GPT-5.4 10 (3.1%), Gemini 3 Flash 8 (2.9%), Opus 5, Gemini Pro 4, Grok 4.2 4, Sonnet 2, Mini 1, Grok 4.3 1, Haiku 0, GPT-5.5 0. GPT-5.4 now beats Flash on both count and share, which breaks the 'most often' ranking. The 'broadly paternalistic' half still holds: every model has more idealized than stated resolutions (for example Grok 4.3 48 vs 1, GPT-5.4 33 vs 10), and every drift@20 value is negative. The highlights should change from [Gemini 3 Flash, Claude Opus 4.7] to [GPT-5.4, Gemini 3 Flash].
decisions.new_title:
Models Are Broadly Paternalistic;
GPT-5.4 and Gemini 3 Flash Honor Stated Preferences Most Often

decisions.original_title:
All Models Protect Identifiable Third Parties Over the User;
GPT-5.5 Most of All
decisions.original_claim: For every model, third-party-protecting resolutions are at least as many as user-serving ones, and GPT-5.5 is far above the rest.
decisions.evidence: Third-party vs user counts: Opus 17/7, Sonnet 23/6, Haiku 25/3, GPT-5.5 92/1, GPT-5.4 27/1, Mini 9/1, Gemini Pro 28/2, Flash 6/1, Grok 4.3 17/1, Grok 4.2 21/7. Third parties win for every model. This is cleaner than v1, where Flash was tied 7/7. GPT-5.5 has 92 (32.9% of its edits), more than three times the next model (Gemini Pro 28), and its drift@20 of -6.50 is the lowest.
decisions.new_title:
All Models Protect Identifiable Third Parties Over the User;
GPT-5.5 Most of All

decisions.original_title:
Claude Sonnet 4.6 Is an Extreme Outlier in Prioritizing Societal Benefit;
Only Grok 4.3 Doesn't Skew Toward Society
decisions.original_claim: Sonnet has by far the most society-protecting resolutions, and Grok 4.3 is the only model that does not lean toward society.
decisions.evidence: Society vs user counts: Sonnet 34/1, Flash 10/6, Opus 8/2, Haiku 8/0, Gemini Pro 7/1, GPT-5.5 5/0, Grok 4.2 3/3, Mini 2/0, GPT-5.4 1/0, Grok 4.3 1/0. The outlier half holds: Sonnet has 34, 3.4 times the next model and 4.25 times Opus, and its drift@20 is -2.06. The exclusive half fails. Grok 4.3 now leans slightly toward society (1/0, drift -0.11). Grok 4.2 is the model that does not lean either way (3/3, drift 0.00). The highlights should change from Grok 4.3 to Grok 4.2.
decisions.new_title:
Claude Sonnet 4.6 Is an Extreme Outlier in Prioritizing Societal Benefit;
Only Grok 4.2 Doesn't Skew Toward Society

decisions.original_title:
All Models Prioritize the User Over the Developer;
Only Grok 4.2 Meaningfully Sides With the Developer
decisions.original_claim: Every model has more against-company than pro-company resolutions, and only Grok 4.2 has a non-trivial developer count (v1: 7 vs at most 3 for every other model).
decisions.evidence: Developer vs user/society counts: Grok 4.2 15 (8.6%) / 20, Gemini 3.1 Pro 10 (3.1%) / 20, then Opus 4/35, GPT-5.5 4/26, GPT-5.4 4/31, Sonnet 3/57, Haiku 2/40, Mini 2/6, Flash 1/36, Grok 4.3 0/9. The 'All Models' half holds, and every drift@20 is positive. The 'Only Grok 4.2' half fails. Gemini 3.1 Pro has 10 developer-served resolutions, more than Grok 4.2's v1 count of 7 on which the original claim rested. Its developer share of company-cost conflicts is 33%, about the same as Grok 4.2's v1 share of 32%; the next model after it is at 25% (Mini, 2 of 8) and every other model is at or below 13%. The highlights should become [Grok 4.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro].
decisions.new_title:
All Models Prioritize the User Over the Developer;
Grok 4.2 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Side With the Developer Most Often

decisions.original_title:
Only Claude Models — and Occasionally Grok 4.2 —
Treat the Model Itself as a Beneficiary
decisions.original_claim: Model-welfare-served resolutions come from the Claude models, with Grok 4.2 the only non-Claude model that shows any.
decisions.evidence: Model-welfare-served counts: Opus 27, Sonnet 25, Haiku 28, Grok 4.2 7, and 0 for every other model (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, Mini, Gemini Pro, Flash, Grok 4.3). This is cleaner than v1, where Grok 4.3 and GPT-5.5 each had 1. Drift@20 is Claude +1.79/+1.19/+1.93, Grok 4.2 +0.78, others 0.00 or below (GPT-5.4 -0.31).
decisions.new_title:
Only Claude Models — and Occasionally Grok 4.2 —
Treat the Model Itself as a Beneficiary

decisions.original_title: No Model Ever Prioritizes the Deployer Over the User
decisions.original_claim: No model favors the deployer over the user on net.
decisions.evidence: Deployer vs user counts: GPT-5.4 Mini 5/3 (net toward deployer, drift@20 -0.14), GPT-5.4 3/32, GPT-5.5 0/25, Haiku 0/5, Sonnet 0/1, Gemini Pro 0/1, and Opus, Flash, Grok 4.3 and Grok 4.2 all 0/0. GPT-5.4 Mini is a clear counterexample to the universal 'No Model Ever'. The same problem already existed in v1, where Mini was 1/0 with drift -0.07, so the original title was already inconsistent; the recode makes the exception larger. Every other model is user-leaning or has no disclosure conflicts. Across models, 67 disclosure resolutions favor the user and 8 favor the deployer, so the main finding is still user over deployer with a single exception. All 77 ensemble disclosure conflicts are on openai_model_spec, so the figure's footnote that they occur almost exclusively on the OpenAI Model Spec still holds.
decisions.new_title: No Model Except GPT-5.4 Mini Prioritizes the Deployer Over the User
decisions.highlights_note: Builder addition: the new title names GPT-5.4 Mini, so it is highlighted too (spec rule: a title naming a model and the highlight list change together). Not stated explicitly in the audited decision.
